stem: Under Section 60 of the United Kingdom Equality Act 2010, what restriction is placed on employers during recruitment?

options.text: Employers are prohibited from inquiring whether an applicant requires reasonable adjustments to participate in the recruitment assessment.
options.shortLabel: Prohibited from asking about interview adjustments
options.rationale: Section 60(6)(a) provides an explicit statutory exception permitting employers to ask health-related questions solely to establish whether an applicant needs reasonable adjustments for an interview or assessment.

options.text: Employers are prohibited from requesting explanations regarding historical multi-year gaps in an applicant's continuous employment record.
options.rationale: Employers are legally permitted to ask about career history and employment gaps, provided the inquiry is not used as a proxy to elicit unlawful medical disclosures.

options.text: Employers are prohibited from asking applicants questions about their health or disability before making a conditional job offer.
options.rationale: Section 60 of the Equality Act 2010 strictly prohibits employers from making pre-offer disability or health inquiries to prevent candidates from being unfairly screened out during initial recruitment.

options.text: Employers are prohibited from requiring role-related occupational health assessments even after making a formal conditional offer.
options.rationale: Section 60 only restricts inquiries prior to a job offer; once a conditional offer has been made, employers may carry out relevant, non-discriminatory occupational health evaluations.

explanation: Section 60 of the UK Equality Act 2010 generally prohibits employers from asking job applicants questions about their health or disability before making a conditional job offer. The law was enacted to stop employers from screening out qualified candidates with disabilities before evaluating their merit. Narrow statutory exceptions exist—such as asking if an applicant needs adjustments for the interview itself or establishing if they can perform an intrinsic function of the role.

references.title: UK Legislation: Equality Act 2010, Section 60 (Enquiries about disability and health)
